svg.text: RAID Levels Comparison — CompTIA A+ Exam Reference
Redundant Array of Independent Disks — All Testable RAID Levels
JBOD — Just a Bunch of Disks
EXAM KEY FACTS — CompTIA A+ RAID Summary
• RAID 0 = Speed ONLY, no fault tolerance. One drive fails = ALL data lost.
• RAID 1 = Exact mirror/copy. Simplest redundancy. Uses 2 drives minimum.
• RAID 5 = Most popular for servers. Distributed parity. Needs minimum 3 drives. Survives 1 failure.
• RAID 6 = Like RAID 5 but with DOUBLE parity. Survives 2 failures. Needs minimum 4 drives.
• RAID 10 (1+0) = Mirrors first, then stripes. Best performance WITH redundancy. Needs 4+ drives (even number).
• JBOD = NOT real RAID. Drives are independent or concatenated. No performance gain, no redundancy.
• Hardware RAID (dedicated controller) vs Software RAID (OS-managed) — Hardware is faster but more expensive.
• Hot spare = Standby drive that auto-rebuilds when an active drive fails.
